title: Unbounded Buffer Allocation in Network Streams
platform_conditions: Swift runtime semantics (Data, streams); applies wherever Swift runs, including iOS/macOS clients and server-side Swift services
security_mechanism: Data(capacity:) reserves the requested capacity up front, so a length taken from a header ('content-length', a protocol length prefix) turns a few attacker bytes into a multi-gigabyte allocation — the memory commit fails or the process is OOM-killed before any data arrives. read loops that append into Data without a cap have the same effect for compressed or chunked bodies, and a decompression step (zlib/Compression framework) multiplies the amplification. On server-side Swift the blocking variant is CPU: a synchronous read or a large JSON decode on the event-loop thread stalls every concurrent connection while the allocation/parse completes.

source_sink_clues.source: Declared lengths in protocol headers, chunked/compressed bodies, and length prefixes in binary payloads from clients.
source_sink_clues.sink: Data(capacity: remoteSize) / Array(repeating:count:) sized from external lengths; read loops appending into Data/String with no byte budget; decompression without output limits; unbounded request-body reads before the Content-Length cap is enforced

tracking_guards: Check every input-derived length is compared to a fixed constant before allocation; check reads accumulate incrementally with a total-byte budget that aborts the connection; check decompression tracks output size and stops at the limit; check the framework's body-size limit is configured for server frameworks rather than left at 'unlimited'.
not_candidate_when: The transport layer already rejects bodies above a small cap before the handler runs and that cap is enforced on every path, the allocation size is a compile-time constant, or the stream is consumed incrementally with an enforced output budget.
synthetic_safe_example: guard remoteSize <= MAX_LIMIT else { return }; var buf = Data(capacity: remoteSize)
public_references: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html
CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html
